name: Five Crowns
summary: Rummy-style card game over 11 rounds where rotating wild cards increase and lowest total score wins.
rules_text: Two 58-card decks are combined. Each has 5 suits (stars, hearts, clubs, spades, diamonds) with 3-K plus 3 Jokers. Jokers are always wild. Each round r, r+2 cards are dealt: round 1 =3 cards and 3s are wild, round 2=4 cards and 4s wild, up to round 11=13 cards and Kings wild. Remaining cards form draw pile, top card starts discard. On turn, player draws top of draw OR top of discard, then tries to form entire hand into books (3+ same rank) and/or runs (3+ consecutive same suit) using wilds anywhere. Hand stays hidden until going out. To go out, on your turn after drawing, meld all cards except one discard face up. Then each other player gets one final turn to meld what they can. Unmelded cards score face value, Jack 11, Queen 12, King 13, current wild 20, Joker 50. Lowest total after 11 rounds wins.
rating_reason: Rummy-style 11-round card game with hidden hands strategic
reasons: dropped: too complex: Five Crowns' essence is a long escalating sequence of hands (3 to 13 cards, rotating wilds) over a 116-card deck, with a combinatorial meld search in every hand. That needs hundreds of turns, large per-card hidden state and multi-step turns far beyond 40 rounds, 4 choices per round and 3 hidden elements. Any cut short enough to build becomes a luck-dominated mini-rummy rather than Five Crowns.
